application_to_platform_contracts.business_promise: Keep a future Podinfo release explainable from reviewed source to immutable artifact, promotion decision and recovery decision.
application_to_platform_contracts.failure_behavior: Missing provenance, immutable artifact identity or explicit promotion evidence keeps every runtime action pending.
application_to_platform_contracts.future_evidence: A later approved phase would provide build, scan, SBOM, digest, plan, promotion and rollback identifiers tied to one source revision.

application_to_platform_contracts.business_promise: Give each future delivery and runtime action a bounded identity without placing infrastructure credentials in the application.
application_to_platform_contracts.failure_behavior: An unnamed principal, broad permission, embedded credential or missing revocation owner blocks the documented release path.
application_to_platform_contracts.future_evidence: A later approved phase would record principal IDs, authorization tests, secret references, rotation results and revocation evidence without secret values.

application_to_platform_contracts.business_promise: Describe one approved, least-exposed path to a future application route while retaining explicit denied paths.
application_to_platform_contracts.failure_behavior: No hostname, certificate owner or reviewed source-to-destination path means the application remains unreachable by design.
application_to_platform_contracts.future_evidence: A later approved phase would provide DNS, TLS, ingress, positive-path and denied-path results tied to the application release.

application_to_platform_contracts.business_promise: Make ownership, dependencies, expected service, escalation and recovery understandable before a future release decision.
application_to_platform_contracts.failure_behavior: Missing owner, dependency, SLO intent, escalation path or recovery decision keeps documentation review open and future acceptance unavailable.
application_to_platform_contracts.future_evidence: A later approved phase would provide a service record, measured SLI/SLO, alert route, exercised runbook and acceptance decision.

application_to_platform_contracts.business_promise: Let a future operator connect user health, service signals and incidents back to the exact application change.
application_to_platform_contracts.failure_behavior: Signals without project and release identity cannot support acceptance; missing or ambiguous telemetry keeps the release unaccepted.
application_to_platform_contracts.future_evidence: A later approved phase would link metrics, logs, traces, alerts and health decisions to source, artifact and release identifiers.

application_to_platform_contracts.business_promise: Describe a bounded future workload that uses the existing application cluster without adding infrastructure or broadening trust.
application_to_platform_contracts.failure_behavior: No approved digest, namespace boundary, pod security, resource decision or recovery plan means no cluster action is permitted.
application_to_platform_contracts.future_evidence: A later approved phase would provide render, policy, rollout, health, exposure and rollback evidence from the existing cluster.
